title: Annular variation of the triangular Hilbert transform at the symmetric point
coverage:
I read every section: introduction, preliminaries, matrix, heat, smooth, frequency, rough, completion and consequences. I checked the following by hand.
(1) Mixed trace inequality. Every closed 3-walk on M with zero diagonal blocks is a triangle, so tr((DM)^3)=6Re tau. A_v=MP_vM=T_v and K_v=R_v^*D_vR_v. The cost reduction E>=Q/2 holds. The cubic expansion cases (smallest index once, twice, three times) give A+3E+3sqrt(AE)<=5(A/2+E)<=5Q. The phase-rotation unitaries are correct. The complex-insertion constant 20/3 is correct.
(2) Order comparison and Loewner-Heinz; joint convexity through the variational formula and sqrt(avg T)>=avg sqrt T; insertion bound; rank-change gradient bound.
(3) Heat identities: 2 d_sigma g = d_p^2 g; T_v is linear in the row density and S_v is linear in each column density. The plane identity d_d^2 J_v equals the integral of d_{p_i}^2 e_v for every i, and also the integral of Z_v by changing chart. The neighbor comparison Y_{w+1,w}+Y_{w-1,w}<=sqrt2 V_w holds (T_w<=2 diag(A^*A,B^*B), block extraction, A^*A<=S_{w+1}). The coefficients for rates (1,1.1,1.1) are -0.151 and -0.393, both negative. The initial-energy grid mass bound holds.
(4) Repeated masks: the row and column norm bounds for the switched entries in R_0 and R_1 are correct. The Gaussian expectations under w_0(i)w_1(j) dpi_0 are correct, including the variance s0+s1+s2 for p_2. Maximal majorants and Hoelder give n(n0^3+n0^2(n1+n2)). Normalizing to (n^{-1/2},1,1) gives sqrt n.
(5) Smooth kernel: the insertion k_s/g_{lambda s} is bounded; (R^b)^*DR^b=sqrt(s)U^n and T^n<=sqrt(lambda)T^b; the convolution over Pi_0 is correct.
(6) Frequency block: the modulated-Gaussian completing-square identity holds. The bounds |alpha(d)|<=C sqrt(theta s) and omega^2 b'<=3q/2 hold. The averaged heat coefficient (2+theta)+(1-theta)=3 is correct, and so is the inequality theta V<=-2dJ+(1/2)sum Y. The single-edge column coefficient is 1. The boundary covariance s[[2theta,-theta],[-theta,3]]<=4s diag(theta,1) holds, with det=s^2 theta(6-theta). The slab sums use sum_k int|mu|^2<=C1^2.
(7) Rough family: f=U/g_{3q}; Var(f''')<=Cm; |xi|^4|f-hat|<=Cm; the L^2 bound via the BV translation inequality; mu=Dc/sqrt n meets both coefficient conditions. The cutoff error is (m/P*)^{1/5}<=C/n with P*=(2+n)^8, and there are O(log n) dyadic blocks.
(8) Odd-kernel telescoping with Psi=phi-Dil_2 phi/2.
(9) Endpoint kernel identity I_{eps,R}=(P(|t|/eps)-P(|t|/R))/t, with psi=-g_3''' and c_0=2g_3''(0) nonzero. Endpoint pairing in dyadic groups: total paired length <=1, at most two unpaired endpoints, at most 2sqrt n groups with m>sqrt n.
(10) Duality/linearization and the rank-dyadic summation to V_r for r>2; maximal and principal-value corollaries; the flat-to-simplex maps.
Numerics:
- Mixed trace: random complex tests give a worst ratio of 0.16 against the bound 5/3.
- Heat flow: a numerical plane integral on a 3-node grid gives -dJ/ds about 1.08 times int sum V, where the paper needs at least c_*=0.075.
- Insertion bound, entry-gradient bound and neighbor comparison: each verified numerically, with max ratios 1.0, 1.0 and 0.71 against a bound of 1.
main_claim: For every r>2, ||V_r(F,G)||_{L^{3/2}} <= C_r ||F||_3 ||G||_3 for the annular r-variation of the triangular Hilbert transform. The paper derives this from the disjoint-annulus count estimate ||S_n||_{3/2} <= C sqrt(n) log(2+n) ||F||_3 ||G||_3. Consequences: the two-endpoint maximal bound, a.e. and norm principal values, and the symmetric (3,3,3) scalar triangular Hilbert form bound (Thiele's Problem 13).
sibling_notes: No sibling entries existed in family 082 when I checked. The paper is self-contained: it proves its matrix and heat estimates itself and does not depend on any companion paper.
